name: Haiti
headline: Haiti: −2.7% growth in 2025, 28.3% inflation, debt 12% of GDP
sections: Haiti is a $32.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 116th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −2.7% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,134 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 20.2% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 28.3% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets. Unemployment stood at 14.9% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 37.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 12% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 22% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.3% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +1.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 16% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 10% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 65.1 years (2024). Population: 12.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
